opening.title: Opening
paragraphs: The fire destroyed most of our food stores, along with most of the passengers' faith.
All we have left is the little food the galley had stocked, a crate of mouthwash Firebreath Ltd. hired us to deliver, and four passengers who don't trust one another.
Let's hope this disaster hasn't robbed you of your brilliant judgment and superb piloting skills.
Calm them. Feed them. Keep everyone steady.

journal: The cause of the fire is still under investigation. I'm inclined to call it an accident, a short circuit in the refrigeration system. But accident or sabotage, the responsibility is mine. The vegetables, the meat, and our poor security guard Daniel Price were all burned into a heap of inedible charcoal. Elias Ward sealed the airlock to the freezer section in time and the fire was contained, but that doesn't mean we survived.

We have a few vegetables and some dry rations left, and Mara Quinn dug some not-quite-so-rotten scraps out of the compost bin. Even if she promises not to waste a single crumb when she cooks so we can hold out longer, there still isn't enough food.
When the time comes, I will make a choice.

Dr. Helena Voss says that if I don't put "Dr." in front of her name in this log, she will happily watch us writhe to death when we all come down with gastroenteritis. She also strongly objects to us eating anything dug out of the compost bin.
"I have treated 312 cases of food poisoning, and half of those patients swore the food 'looked perfectly fresh.'"
Of course, she didn't say it nearly that calmly.

Mason Reed didn't sleep all night. He kept singing the same few folk songs he picked up on his home planet, wandering lap after lap around the cabin and kicking the bottles of mouthwash all over the place. Whoever tells him to get lost and go to bed, he shakes his fist and says he's a free man now, just like everyone else, and has every right to do whatever he pleases.
"A prisoner with no guard is a law-abiding citizen." That's how he put it.

Everyone had a normal, even generous, dinner yesterday, so nobody is at risk of starving just yet. But if I'm blindly overconfident in my own abilities, I could give them an extra meal and make some trouble for myself.
Slept like a baby, if you ignore the four trips to the toilet.
They still call me Captain, but I can't shake the feeling that one of them is going to drive something sharp through my throat while I sleep.
Mara looks a little defeated, because she feels her cooking isn't getting the showcase it deserves. Mind you, she used to toss artichoke leaves straight into the trash.
Mason is still singing those damned songs on repeat. If we make it back alive, I'm hiring him a vocal coach, so the next people stuck with him won't have to suffer like this.

We discussed what this pile of mouthwash might be good for besides fresh breath. First of all, since it's mouthwash, it must contain sugar and alcohol. So we could treat it as an industrial mojito with a lethal dose of mint: stay drunk and keep your teeth pearly white at the same time. Or we could use it as disinfectant. The passengers argued endlessly over those two options. But we did agree on one thing: whatever Firebreath is paying us isn't worth risking our lives to hand this cargo back to them intact.
They haven't shown an ounce of the solidarity you'd hope for in a crisis, but at least I'm still alive. Maybe I should reward them with a little food?

journal.text: I really regret making that deal with Elias. All he did was open the airlock, poke his head in, and say, "Captain, the fire's out." I wanted him to check the wiring for faults, but he just wandered over to central control and glanced at the readings.
No, no, what am I doing, hoping something actually goes wrong? As long as everyone stays alive, if he wants the mouthwash or this whole ship, he can have it.

{name} was very reluctant, but {ta} still took a look into the freezer. Thankfully the fire was completely out. All that was left was warm, stifling air, and {ta} came out drenched in sweat. As for the wiring, {name} said {ta} knew absolutely nothing about it. If something serious had broken, we'd just have to sit here and wait to die.
Better to risk the oxygen system failing and all of us suffocating than to let a single crew member get hurt. What a merciful captain I am, right?

journal: Mara is desperate to get her hands on some French T55 flour, a few Périgord truffles, and a big slab of A5 Nagasaki fillet, just to show us her beef Wellington. Elias and Mason kept asking her what to drink with it. They'd never heard of a single one of the names she gave them, but just knowing they stood for the very finest alcohol got them all worked up.
"Lucky for us we can't get any of those ingredients. Otherwise, after all this time, all that butter would give us 'atherosclerosis' and we'd drop dead."
Dr. Voss said this while chewing on an artichoke leaf.
"Maybe not Elias and Mason. They'll do something stupid while drunk and die in ways no normal person could ever imagine."
"Maybe we'll all die, but at least we're free!" Mason raised a bottle of mouthwash high.
3.allocation_text: Time to hand out supplies, Captain. (That's me.)

journal: Good news: according to the navigation system, the nearest habitable planet, Tahiti, is only 26 days away!
More good news! We have more than enough fuel to reach it!
Bad news: we don't have enough food. Before we reach that mysterious utopia, we'll have turned into five very confident skeletons.
A third piece of good news: they'll be able to identify the dead by the clothes we're wearing.

Mason has been explaining why he should count as a "legal citizen." His criminal record shows he went to a protected nature-reserve planet in Centaurus several times to poach a kind of giant snail, and repeatedly contacted an interstellar trader suspected of smuggling. But he insists it was all just "self-defense."
"A snail the size of a mountain! The smallest tooth on its radula could slice you clean in half!"

Everyone nodded along, pretending to buy it. Only Elias said flat out that he's a bastard who'll weasel his way out of anything. Thankfully neither of them had been drinking the mouthwash, so they still had a shred of sense.
Mara is hungry. She says these lousy leaves don't count as real food.
4.allocation_text: So, who gets stuck finishing off these awful leaves tonight?

sawdust_meal.title: Sawdust Supper
description: Elias came up with a novel kind of food: sawdust! Why not? It grows out of the ground and gets watered by the rain like any other part of a plant, so why can't we eat it? He says that when the workers breaking ground in those remote star systems run out of food, they mix a little flour with the dust they saw off the scaffolding. Our miserable digestive systems can't process cellulose at all, so it would just move into our guts and stay there for a while. And if your stomach is always full, you never need to eat, right?

Dr. Voss pointed out that this is an utterly absurd idea. It's not only irresponsible to our health, it's a grave insult to her as a doctor of medicine. I won't write down her long list of evidence and case studies. Honestly, the real reason is that I didn't remember any of it. Anyway, she suggested using a chemical to break the sawdust down into smaller molecules the human body can digest. It won't turn into a perfectly healthy cookie, but it should at least lower the chance of getting sick.

description.text: Mason swears he'd rather starve than chew on a tree

description: If you trust Elias, he'll add to your Food stores, but the crew may get sick. If you go with Dr. Voss, who knows far more about health, your Food stores will go up a little, with no risk of anyone getting sick.
sawdust_meal.option_nonsense: This is ridiculous! (Mason would want you to do this)
sawdust_meal.complaint: Elias doesn't get why, at a time like this, you're still going along with some other idiot's nonsense. He and his fellow workers got through hard times exactly this way, and he doesn't see any of them coming down with cancer or heart disease. If you're going to turn down the wisdom of the working class, the least you can do is give him the compensation he's owed.
sawdust_meal.complaint_give_in: Damn it, let him have his way (go with Elias's plan)

thief.title: Thief!
thief.description: {name} stole a big portion of food and got caught red-handed trying to hide it. I don't think we can blame {ta_obj}. Anyone this hungry would do the same. But the one thing we can't accept is that {ta} refuses to hand the food over! Should we use our fists to persuade {ta_obj} to share it with everyone, trade {ta_obj} a bottle of mouthwash for it, or just let {ta_obj} have a good meal?
thief.option_force: Persuade by force (small chance someone gets hurt)
thief.option_mason: Have Mason deal with it (nothing happens)

alcohol_distill.title: Distilled Alcohol
alcohol_distill.description: Dr. Voss caught me trying to treat {name}'s wound. She "tactfully" pointed out that I hadn't separated the sugar out of the mouthwash, which will make the wound fester so it never fully heals. The only real fix is to admit she's the most educated person on this ship, and give her two bottles of mouthwash so she can distill alcohol pure enough for the job.
alcohol_distill.option_accept: Fine, Dr. Voss, I admit you're much smarter than me (Mouthwash -2, back to Healthy)
alcohol_distill.option_refuse: Forget it. The captain is always the smartest person on the ship. (nothing happens)
alcohol_distill.option_mason: Tell Mason someone called his captain an idiot (Mouthwash -2, back to Healthy, and you don't have to admit anything to Dr. Voss)

mason_guard.title: Does He Count as a Guard?
mason_guard.description: We're clearly a mess. Just last night, Mason found out that selfish {name} had been secretly keeping a portion of food the whole time, with no intention of sharing it. Nice work, Mason. I just hope next time he uses his fists a little less and his brain a little more.

octopus.title: Our Squishy Roommate
octopus.description: We heard strange noises coming from the air vent. When we pried the wire mesh open, we found a giant octopus! We need a brave soul to drive out this uninvited guest, or turn it into our dinner. The only problem is that this stretch of vent leads into cold storage, so if we don't want our crew electrocuted, maybe we should send someone who knows the ship.

send_options.mason: Mason Reed (these three: high chance of injury, small chance of death)

jason_knock.title: Someone Even Stranger Than These Four?
description: Something is knocking on our airlock. Maybe we're just hearing things. Maybe it's the ghosts of the people we threw out the airlock, come back for us. Or maybe it's some supernatural creature that doesn't need oxygen and can move freely through the vacuum. Thank goodness, it can communicate, and it even speaks English! Later we figured out that he's just an ordinary human who happens not to need oxygen and can move freely through the vacuum. His name is Josan, and he desperately needs alcohol. He brought us a little food as a show of good faith and asked us to let him in.
jason_knock.option_allow: Let him in (Josan comes aboard, -1 Mouthwash every 2 days)

jason_fed_up.title: We've Had Enough!
jason_fed_up.description: All right, this is beyond ridiculous. In all the days Josan has been here, he hasn't lifted a finger. All he does is drink our mouthwash. Elias points out that this is naked exploitation and oppression. That hard-won batch of mouthwash cost us the whole crew's reputation, plus the compensation Firebreath is about to come after us for. Mara keeps worrying that he'll get drunk, open the airlock and throw us out one by one. In short, everyone agrees that letting Josan in was a complete and utterly absurd mistake. Do you want to send someone to ruthlessly kick him out and salvage what little reputation you have left, or let him keep wasting all our mouthwash?

debt_crisis.title: Debt Crisis
debt_crisis.description: I picked up a signal from another ship. They turned out to be Firebreath people. But those selfish bastards have no intention of rescuing us. They came to find out why that crate of mouthwash never arrived. I told them there had been a fire on board, our food had burned, and we were about to starve. All they kept asking was how we plan to pay for a crate of mouthwash worth less than a hundred dollars in total. We have nothing, and their solution is for us to send one crew member to work for them. They promise to send that crew member home once the debt is paid off. Who should we send to contribute a little muscle to our finances? Or do we grab our weapons and drive off these bastards who'd leave us to die?
debt_crisis.option_fight: [TBD] Grab our weapons and drive them off
debt_crisis.leave_elias: The truth is, I've always offered Elias extremely generous terms, [TBD]
debt_crisis.leave_mara: [TBD] Mara left with the Firebreath crew.
debt_crisis.leave_helena: [TBD] Dr. Voss left with the Firebreath crew.
debt_crisis.leave_mason: [TBD] Mason left with the Firebreath crew.
debt_crisis.fight_result: [TBD] We grabbed our weapons and drove the Firebreath crew off.
